S041-01.notes: Colon after the independent clause 'inventors are largely forgotten' introduces the list. B leaves a fragment after the semicolon; C ('which the folding ladder...') and D ('and the folding ladder...') make no sense grammatically. All options are well formed.

S041-02.notes: The list items contain internal commas, and the next item ends in 'Osaka;', so the semicolon separator is needed after 'Lisbon'. B blurs the item boundary, and so do C and D. Exactly one answer works.

S041-03.notes: The opening dash before 'made' has to be closed by a matching dash before 'was'. A, C and D each mismatch the dash or leave it unclosed.

S041-04.notes: A colon after the complete clause introduces 'fresh water' as the single resource. A and C leave a fragment ('fresh water, which had to be...'), and B gives an ungrammatical relative clause.

S041-05.notes: An introductory dependent 'Because' clause takes a comma before the main clause. A and B can't be used after a dependent clause. D is a garden-path run-on ('during shipping the team...').

S041-06.notes: 'However' interrupts the clause between subject and verb, so it takes paired commas. C leaves a fragment after the semicolon ('however, showed...'), A lacks the closing comma, and D lacks the opening comma.
